strings.name: Hillary Clinton
strings.role: Former US secretary of state · Presidential nominee
strings.summary: Clinton moved from law and children’s advocacy into national politics as first lady, senator for New York and secretary of state. She promoted women’s rights in Beijing and became the first female presidential nominee of a major US party in 2016, winning the popular vote but losing the Electoral College. A failed health reform effort, her Iraq War vote and private email server controversy also shaped her career.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: A former US secretary of state and senator, she became the first female presidential nominee of a major US party and has had a lasting influence on public policy.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Wellesley College, BA (1969); Yale Law School, JD (1973)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Women’s rights advocacy
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Her 1995 Beijing speech placed women’s rights at the center of international human rights debate.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: A historic nomination
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Became the first woman nominated for president by a major US political party in 2016.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Received the Presidential Medal of Freedom
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Recognized for her long public service with one of the highest US civilian honors.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Lost the presidential election
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Won the national popular vote but lost the Electoral College to Donald Trump.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Email investigation findings
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The FBI criticized careless handling of classified material but recommended no charges; the dispute shadowed her campaign.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Became secretary of state
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Led US diplomacy in the Obama administration until February 2013.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Supported Iraq war authorization
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Voted as a senator to authorize military action and later acknowledged the decision was a mistake.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Entered the Senate
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Took office for New York after the 2000 election and won reelection in 2006.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Beijing women’s rights speech
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Argued at the UN World Conference on Women that women’s rights are universal human rights.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Led a health reform effort
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Chaired the health reform task force as first lady; the proposal did not pass Congress.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completed her legal education
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Graduated from Yale Law School and pursued children’s advocacy, legal aid and legal work in Arkansas.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Chicago
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Chicago and grew up in nearby Park Ridge.
